segments.text: Come in, take a seat. It's Mr. Tobias Hargreaves, is that right? Just checking I've pulled up the correct record.
Yes, that's right. Sorry, I'm a bit early. I wasn't sure how long the car park would take, and I didn't want to be late.
Not at all, you're exactly on time as far as I'm concerned. This is your review for the anxiety. How have the last few months been?
Mixed, I suppose. Better than last year. But I've been avoiding team meetings again, and I keep worrying that means I'm sliding backwards. Is that what it means?
Let's not jump to that yet. You're avoiding the team meetings. Tell me how long that's been going on.
Three months, roughly. Since we got a new manager who likes everyone to speak up. I just find a reason to be somewhere else.
So it's been about three months, and it started when the new manager arrived. What happens in you when you picture walking into one?
My stomach drops, and I start rehearsing what I'd say, over and over. Then it feels easier just to skip it. Which is awful, isn't it?
It's very human, and it's good that you can see the pattern. What about the panic attacks you had last year? Where are those now?
Oh, those have gone. Honestly gone, I haven't had one since the summer. I keep expecting one to come back, though.
So the panic attacks are gone, but the avoidance of meetings is still there. Let's check your tablets. Which ones are you on at the moment?
Sertraline, 100 milligrams once a day, in the morning. And the omeprazole, 20 milligrams, also every morning. Then propranolol, 10 milligrams, only when I've got a presentation.
Sertraline, omeprazole and propranolol as needed, thank you for being so clear. Any problems taking them, any side effects that bother you?
No, nothing really. I just worry about being on them for so long. Is it normal to still need them after this long?
Many people stay on sertraline for a good while, and it's doing a job for you. I've got in your notes social anxiety, reflux and eczema. Is that all still accurate?
Yes, that's all of it. Though the eczema is mostly quiet now, just my hands in winter.
And any operations in the past, anything at all?
Only my tonsils, when I was nine. I don't remember much, just the ice cream afterwards.
That's the best part, of course. Now I need to ask about some darker thoughts, which I ask everybody. Any thoughts of harming yourself?
No, no. Never like that. It's more that I feel stupid and ashamed, not that I want to... no.
I'm glad you told me, and feeling ashamed is something we can work on together. And when your heart does race, any chest pain or fainting?
No, no chest pain and no fainting. It's only that nervous thumping, and then it passes. Is that normal?
It's a common pattern, and it's reassuring that there's no pain. Now a few quick questions about the rest of your body. Any problems with your breathing?
No, my breathing's fine. I even jogged up the stairs this morning because I was worried about being late.
Okay. And your stomach and digestion on the omeprazole, any trouble there?
No, that's all settled, thankfully. Nothing at all.
Good. Do you have any allergies to medicines or anything else?
No, none that I know of. I was always asked this at the dentist and never had anything.
Great. Let me take your measurements now. Blood pressure is 124 over 78.
Pulse is 84 and regular. Temperature is 36.5 degrees. Oxygen saturation is 99 percent.
Is my pulse too fast? It's always racing when I come to the doctor's.
84 is perfectly normal, even a little relaxed. Your weight is 78 kilograms, and your breathing rate is 14 a minute.
Hold your hands out for me, fingers spread. Your hands are steady, there's no tremor, and no sweating on the palms.
That's a relief. I thought they'd be shaking.
They're not. Now, I'd like to arrange a blood test, to check your thyroid and blood count. Anxiety can sometimes be mimicked or worsened by those.
Do you think something's wrong with my thyroid? Is that why I'm like this?
No, I don't think that, it's simply a sensible thing to check at a review. I'd also like to book an ECG, since you take propranolol.
All right. Is that painful? I hate needles.
The ECG is just stickers on your chest, and the blood test takes seconds. The receptionist will give you the forms on your way out.
Thank you, doctor. I feel a bit calmer now, to be honest.
Good. Keep taking the tablets as you are, and be kind to yourself about the meetings. Take care.
